chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: Critics who discover artists
summary: Critics are uncritical of Coltrane after attacking him; who discovered Ornette and Roland Kirk.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: That's kind of a bridge to what I was going to ask about. The critics -- once again, it was like Arnette. Once they went through the period when they were putting him down because they didn't like the sound or whatever, they were uncritical. He really could do nothing wrong.
So I was wondering, you were one of the first of the musicians to answer the critics back, in Downbeat and places like that. And in the years you've been in this,
Yeah, but I'm not a critic.
I know. That's probably why you got better, because you're broader than a critic. A critic always wants to discover somebody.
Like, Bessie Errine discovered Nesuhi Ertegun Artie Ornette Coleman, as far as I know. He brought him out to -- what's that, Brandeis?
Oh, no, brought him out to the place in the Berkshires, that school -- I remember that school of music. But, actually, Les Lee Konig found Ornette first, a guy in contemporary records.
A Chicago critic. Wrote a big article about him.
